metadata.note: The Ohio and Mississippi (Cincinnati - Vincennes - East St. Louis, its Louisville Branch and its Springfield Division) and its successors the Baltimore and Ohio Southwestern (1893) and the Baltimore and Ohio (1900), plus the Springfield and Illinois South Eastern before 1875. Drawn from the research report research/branches/ohio_and_mississippi_railway.txt (historical-trains repo, 2026-10-30), obeying its drawable: spans. Features are split at every operator change (S&ISE > O&M 1875, O&M > B&OSW 1893, B&OSW > B&O 1900; Rule 4) and at every terminal alignment change (Cincinnati 1883 and 1933; St. Louis 1875, 1894 and 1940; Louisville Branch 1887; Rule 2), sharing geometry where the alignment is the same. No feature before 1875 crosses the Mississippi.

metadata.not_yet_sourced: OPEN ENDS/STARTS - these years are the last or first CONFIRMED year, not a known end or opening: Louisville Branch starts 1875 (opened 1867-1875, year unknown); Springfield - Pana starts 1870 (PS&NW building from 1865); Pana - Shawneetown starts 1874; Flora - Shawneetown B&OSW ends 1896 (passengers gone by Sept 1951, year unknown; no B&O-era feature); Springfield Division B&O ends 1947 (Wikipedia alone gives 24 Mar 1951). Also unsourced: the exact O&M > B&OSW handover month; the 1887 Louisville routing change beyond Fowler; when local service on Watson - Jeffersonville ended (1887-1951); the date of the Lebanon / O'Fallon former route and of the ~1900 Indiana relocations; the site of the first East St. Louis riverfront depot; every headway and avg_speed_kmh.
metadata.source_conflicts: 1) O&M absorbed by the B&OSW in 1893 (Wikipedia, both articles) vs "formally merged" 1900 (american-rails); drawn split at 1893. 2) Louisville Branch end: chicagorailfan's Louisville page says passenger service ended in 1960 but shows a 1971 board with B&O times, and Fowler dates Central Station 1887>1961; drawn to 1960, 1960-1971 NOT drawn pending a 1960s timetable. 3) Flora passenger end: NRHP form (via Wikipedia) 1973 and KPC News 1972 vs the B&O's last intercity trains on 30 April 1971; main line drawn to 1971. 4) Gauge conversion 23 July 1871 (Wikipedia) vs 13 July 1871 (american-rails); not a drawing issue. 5) S&ISE > O&M 1875: acquisition (Wikipedia) vs reorganization (another history); an operator change either way.
metadata.branches_deliberately_omitted: Bedford Branch (Rivervale - Bedford, opened Sept 1893): drawable NONE, no confirmable passenger year. Watson - Jeffersonville after 1887: drawable NONE, no passenger year confirmed after 1887 (freight-only by 1951). Flora - Shawneetown B&O era (1900+): drawable NONE. Beardstown - Springfield before 1875 (S&ISE era): drawable NONE, no pre-1875 evidence. The ex-CH&D Cincinnati - Hamilton B&O line: never an O&M line, out of scope.
metadata.freight_only_excluded: Nothing freight-only is drawn: Flora - Shawneetown, Beardstown - Flora and Watson - Jeffersonville were freight-only by Sept 1951 (Official Guide Tables 51, 56, 98); the CSX Indiana/Illinois Subdivision freight afterlife after 1971 is not drawn.

segments.note: Cincinnati - Aurora, the first section of the Ohio and Mississippi, opened 1854 (jjakucyk; Fowler dates the Front & Mill depot "1854>1883"). Built to 6 ft broad gauge; converted to standard gauge in a single day in July 1871 (23 July per Wikipedia, 13 July per american-rails; 23 July 1871 was a Sunday). Not a drawing break. Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.

segments.note: Beardstown - Springfield - Pana - Flora under the Baltimore and Ohio (Pana passenger station listed 1901). After the B&O bought the Alton in 1931 its Springfield trains used the ex-Alton station (Fowler "BO service diverted to GMO station 1931>1947"); the Decatur - Springfield trains ended in WWII, leaving a single motorcar on this line (Wikipedia, Springfield Union Station). END IS OPEN: 1947 is the last year CONFIRMED by two sources (Fowler and Wikipedia). Wikipedia alone (uncited) says the motorcar ran until 24 March 1951, and the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 56 ("Freight Service only") shows only that passengers were gone by Sept 1951. Not drawn past 1947; extend to 1951 only if a 1948-50 timetable shows the motorcar. Freight continued (Beardstown - Springfield abandoned 1979, the rest by 1983-85). Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.
